name: Japan
notes: House of Representatives: 289 single-member constituencies (first-past-the-post) + 176 PR seats in 11 regional blocs (D'Hondt, no threshold). Baseline: the 8 February 2026 snap election (LDP 316 seats, a two-thirds majority). District winners are projected by plurality from the 2026 top-two baselines (winner + runner-up shares; no full candidate lists). The swing is anchored on the party-support baseline at the 2026 election (the average of the 11 first polls after 8 Feb 2026: LDP 37.0, DRP/CRA 7.3, ...), the same measure as the current polls - support vs support, not support vs vote. The polls' raw shares (including 'no party') are used: they track actual vote shares closely (pre-election support ~40 vs the 36.72 actual), so no undecided redistribution is applied to the averages; instead the map's district shares are display-normalised (districtNormalize) so the ~30pp no-party share does not read as a ~50% 'other' - the no-party/undecided are assumed to break proportionally, the projected winners are unchanged, and the 2026 result view stays exact. The PR tier uses per-bloc D'Hondt from the same anchor; the real allocation also reallocates seats forfeited by list exhaustion (not modelled) and the official per-party PR totals are 67/42/20/16/15/11/4/1. Party names follow the 2026 realignment: the Centrist Reform Alliance became the Democratic Reform Party (DRP, 民主改革の会, split 17 Sep 2026) and Reiwa Shinsengumi became the Party of Life. Geometry: the Commons 2024 constituency map (data-name labels; Akita unlabeled, Wakayama-2 typo and the Shimane-1 inset leader line handled; 2022 reapportionment cuts included). Next election: by February 2030.
